articles.title: National Grid to site biggest substation in UK near planned Teesside datacentre
articles.summary: New electricity generating capacity would enable north-east to attract investment for large-scale AI infrastructure. National Grid has taken a step towards building Britain’s biggest electricity substation on Teesside, which could supply power to a vast neighbouring datacentre as the UK races to…
body: Last week, the company agreed to purchase 29.5 hectares (73 acres) of land at Dorman Point on a site owned by Teesworks, a local private-public partnership. The deal was first reported by Sky News.

The deal followed reports last year that the UK government had picked Teesworks as the site for a new artificial intelligence datacentre, and planning applications had been submitted for a project that would span nearly 500,000 sq metres.

The deal “reflects the constructive work between all those involved to enable this vital infrastructure … and will support the growth of AI and digital technologies, and enable the region’s next phase of industrial and economic development”, Matt Pearce, the head of land at National Grid, said. “We are committed to working closely with our partners to progress the development as quickly as possible,” he added.

Ben Houchen, the mayor of the Tees Valley combined authority, told Sky News: “Everyone who has tried to build a datacentre in this country knows the biggest problem is getting enough power to the site quickly.

articles.title: Binance users withdraw $3.6bn after record crypto hack
articles.summary: The exchange froze transactions in the wake of the incident, which impacted $6.3bn worth of digital assets.
body: Binance customers withdrew a net $3.64bn (£2.72bn) of assets from the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange as it reopened on Sunday following a record hack last week.
Major organisations, including the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), have accused North Korea of being responsible for the cyber-attack, which is said to be the largest hack in history.

The company said it has covered around 95% of the assets stolen in the breach, but that the remaining amount may take longer to source. Binance has repeatedly said it would cover all of the losses linked to the attack.

"Between 06:00 and 15:30 [GMT] on November 1, we processed $4.649 billion in withdrawals and $1.01 billion in deposits, resulting in a net outflow of approximately $3.64 billion," Binance posted on X.

articles.title: NASA hopes the commercial space industry can help save Hubble
articles.summary: Gravity is a cruel mistress, slowly dragging the famed telescope ever closer to its ultimate demise with every day. Hubble is in no immediate danger of burning up in the Earth's atmosphere, but its time will run out in the early to mid 2030s unless its orbit is boosted.
body: The Hubble Space Telescope will come crashing to Earth sometime in the 2030s without a boost.

“Hubble still has important science ahead of it, and we should be looking at every reasonable opportunity to keep it delivering for as long as possible … If there are innovative and cost-effective ways to extend the life of an asset already on orbit, we owe it to the American taxpayer and the scientific community to explore them. Extending Hubble’s life would mean more discoveries, more science, and more opportunities to expand our understanding of the universe.”

articles.title: Flock keeps ignoring requests to cancel its contracts
articles.summary: While more cities are canceling their contracts with Flock Safety, just as many are discovering how difficult that can be in some instances. Plymouth, Minnesota's city council voted to terminate its contract with Flock in September, but failed to respond to the city's request.
body: Cities are canceling Flock contracts, but the company won’t take them down and sometimes is reinstalling them.

“After hearing nothing for more than a week, I directed our staff to disconnect the power cords from the cameras in order to be sure that they are not functioning or recording plates,” Fadden told The Drive.

Roughly 20 miles up the road, Dayton, Minnesota, is having its own issues with Flock. In this instance, the company acknowledged the city’s request and said it would take up to 60 days to remove the equipment. Despite this, Flock reconnected two cameras within the city limits without authorization, and following a specific request from the local police not to complete the work order.

On September 17, 2026, the Police Department was made aware of a maintenance work order produced by Flock. The City notified Flock on September 18, 2026, that the program was on hold, and no work orders were to be completed. Unfortunately, the City’s direction was not followed, and the camera was placed back into service without authorization.

articles.title: AI is stealing Indigenous Australian art and churning out ‘Temu slop’, artist says
articles.summary: Chair of National Gallery’s First Nations advisory group says the technology is undermining artists’ agency and the authenticity of their work. Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.
body: AI is taking First Nations art and turning it into “Temu slop”, the Pitjantjatjara artist Sally Scales has said.

Scales, the chair of the National Gallery of Australia’s First Nations advisory group, says the technology is undermining the agency of First Nations artists and the authenticity of their work and represents a “a theft” of cultural knowledge.

Despite Anthony Albanese’s vow to protect Australian creatives from copyright theft, and the attorney general, Michelle Rowland, saying there are “no plans to weaken copyright protections”, AI has already been trained – without compensation – on the works of well known Australian artists including Kylie Minogue and Nick Cave.

But experts are particularly worried about the risks to Indigenous cultural and intellectual property (ICIP) in a world where AI companies can hoover up anything that may be found online, including songs and paintings that include sacred and cultural knowledge. AI has altered work, removed names and then been sold, an act the peak body for Australian visual artists said was causing “cultural and economic harm”.
points: Chair of National Gallery’s First Nations advisory group says the technology is undermining artists’ agency and the authenticity of their work.

On the one side you have the behemoth that is Grand Theft Auto VI, an experience 13 years in the making, and the sequel to one of the best-selling games in history. Its predecessor, GTA V, has sold a staggering 230 million copies since it launched in 2013, and was re-released across three generations of consoles. Developer Rockstar is a pioneer in the realm of open-world games, dating back to GTA III, and the scale and ambitions of those worlds have steadily grown since then. With GTA V and later Red Dead Redemption 2, the studio’s ideas reached a new level of realism. And the sixth GTA looks poised to eclipse them both, which has created an unprecedented level of demand.

articles.title: Why you should treat charisma as a red flag
articles.summary: Today’s crop of smooth talkers tap directly into a specific evolutionary vulnerability. Here’s how to defend yourself. Recently, I was alone in a bar waiting for a friend. To pass the time, I started chatting to a stranger. He had an easy, confident way of speaking, which I admired.
body: It’s increasingly difficult to ignore how fragmented and bizarre our beliefs have become. We live in our own echo chambers, defined by the channels, feeds and influencers we follow. As a result we can arrive at very polarised conclusions about vaccines, the climate, gender, geopolitics, the shape of the Earth and everything else. Disagreements on topics like these frequently damage relationships, alienate friends and estrange loved ones.

How did things get so bad? I believe the answer is, in part, that we’re constantly exposed to a novel form of charisma. As a psychiatrist, I’ve always been fascinated by this quality: the magnetism that brings out a deep sense of trust, loyalty or enthusiasm in others. The psychology of charisma tells us that it is not necessarily a magic, undefinable X-factor, but rather a set of skills and behaviours. Sometimes people have it naturally, sometimes people learn it.
points: Today’s crop of smooth talkers tap directly into a specific evolutionary vulnerability.

He had an easy, confident way of speaking, which I admired.

articles.title: Apple’s HomeView could add security camera features
articles.summary: Reddit user pdfu found hints hidden in the HomeView 27.2 code that Apple could be adding security camera features to its smart home hub. The strings describe a security camera mode with motion detection, live streaming, and recording options, as well as privacy functions.
body: Code strings in HomeView’s software suggest Apple could launch a Secure Video feature soon.

Supposedly, the video feeds will only be visible to members of the home, and will both show an indicator light and play a sound when either someone is watching the camera feed or when it starts to record. Home members will also get a notification anytime settings are changed for the Secure Video mode. It will also include customizable options for what to detect, stream, or record, based on whether you’re home, away, or asleep.

Some wondered why Apple did not allow HomeView to double as a security camera at launch, and the company hasn’t said anything to suggest the features are coming. But, considering how central privacy is to Apple’s marketing, the company may be waiting to fine-tune those features before launch.

articles.title: 6 Google Maps features that work better on Android Auto vs. CarPlay
articles.summary: You would think that Maps would be the same regardless of your phone's brand, but there are some differences between the Android Auto and CarPlay experiences.
body: I tested Google Maps on both systems in the same car, and Android Auto made several everyday navigation tasks noticeably easier.

Google Maps is available on both Android Auto and Apple CarPlay, but it's not the same experience — even when using the same app in the same car. I performed identical searches, route changes and simple navigation tasks back to back on both systems using the same infotainment screen.

Generally speaking, the fundamentals are close. Both provided me with a speedometer, lane guidance, incident reporting and alternative-route suggestions, as well as the standard controls for avoiding tolls, highways and ferries. The differences were much more apparent after I began using Maps for more than just getting from A to B.

The benefits of Android Auto range from minor interface details to features that still work better there than on Apple's offering. CarPlay does recover a few points, but Google Maps generally feels more at home on Google's own platform. Shocking, I know.

articles.title: How to add and rearrange apps on your Samsung smart TV
articles.summary: Though your Samsung smart TV comes pre-loaded with the most popular streaming apps, you may want to add others and do some reorganizing while you're at it.
body: Smart TVs make it easy to access streaming services as well as self-hosted media servers, such as Plex, without needing to buy an extra device like a streaming stick (though there are other reasons to buy a streaming device when you have a smart TV ). But even if you have a smart TV, you might not be taking full advantage of it. Fortunately, it's easy to add new apps to a Samsung smart TV if the ones you want aren't already included when you first set it up.

If you only need the most popular streaming services, you might not need to do anything to get them running. Samsung smart TVs usually come pre-loaded with the Netflix, YouTube, Disney+, Prime Video and Apple TV apps, though that list can change depending on which apps are available in your particular region. For anything else ( like these free channels for your smart TV ), you'll have to download a new app from a built-in search feature on your TV. And after downloading those apps, you'll probably want to do some rearranging on your home screen.

articles.title: Android Auto could upset your work-life balance with its next update
articles.summary: A hidden toggle buried in the Android Auto app's code isn't functional yet. Here's what it could do, what it might not, and what Google hasn't said so far.
body: A hidden Work Mode tile hints at support for employer-managed apps, but no word on when it might arrive.

Your commute could soon come with a little more office baggage. An Android Authority teardown of Android Auto version 18.0.664204 revealed a Work Mode tile, suggesting Google may be testing new Work Profile controls. The site's team managed to bring up the tile, which lit up a briefcase icon over the app drawer, but tapping the tile didn't do anything.

Supporting Work Profiles could make it easier to join work calls between appointments. Then again, it could also give the office another way to follow you into the car, which isn't exactly everyone's idea of a peaceful drive.
